description: citation (ADR 0031): what a citation looks like, said once for both tiers. The comment gate runs twice — an oxlint rule over the TypeScript tier and a script over the Python one — and both refuse a comment that says which ticket, decision or rule asked for the code, and a string in source that sends the person reading it to a document they cannot open from where they read it. Until this file they each carried the five patterns themselves, so a sixth was two edits that could disagree, and a fifth that drifted would have each gate refusing a different tree. `patterns` is the whole of the agreement, in the order the gates try them: `name` is the words the gate's message puts after *cites*, `pattern` is a regular expression written in the subset both languages read the same way — no flags, because a flag is not part of a pattern string either tier can compile — and `why` says what the pattern is holding. `cites` are the samples a gate must refuse, each with the very text it must quote back; `cites_nothing` are sentences that carry none of the five and must pass, which is how each suite sees that its gate holds no pattern of its own. A sample is written as the parts a suite joins, because a rule tag spelled whole here would be a rule tag written outside the three places the rules allow one; every other sample is a list of one. The TypeScript half compiles this file in `packages/devtools/src/citations.ts` and the Python half in `packages/devtools/python/citations.py`; the oxlint rule, the script and the write-time hook that runs them read those, and neither gate writes a pattern out any more, so a sixth is one edit here. Each tier's contract suite drives its own gate over every sample below: the core suite runs the rule through the throwaway-tree runner (packages/core/test/tier-contract.test.ts) and the worker suite runs the script itself (apps/worker/tests/test_tier_contract.py).
